### ABB Context

- **Parent Composite ABB**: [GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01 — Identity and Access Management Composite ABB](GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01.md)
- **Sibling ABB**: [GUID-SEC-IAM-ID.ME-STRATEGY-2.2.10 — ID.me Identity Proofing Integration ABB](GUID-SEC-IAM-ID.ME-STRATEGY-2.2.10.md) — this document defines the integration pattern for CLEAR as an alternative and complementary CSP; the ID.me ABB covers the government-certified IAL2 proofing path
- **Domain**: Domain 4b — External CSP Integration (Identity Assurance)
- **Capability Statement**: Establishes the architectural integration pattern for leveraging CLEAR (biometric identity platform) as a Credential Service Provider (CSP) to deliver biometric-anchored identity proofing and repeat authentication for member, provider, workforce, and service desk scenarios, mediated through the enterprise Identity Broker. **CLEAR operates exclusively as a CSP. It is not an Identity Provider (IdP), cannot issue enterprise identity session tokens, cannot maintain enterprise authentication state, and cannot serve as a primary authentication authority for any enterprise application. The enterprise Identity Broker is a required architectural component in all CLEAR deployments — not an optional optimization.**

> **Regulatory Scope of This ABB**: CLEAR does not hold Kantara IAL2 accreditation or FedRAMP authorization at the time of this document's authoring. This ABB therefore does not assert equivalence with government-mandated IAL2. See Core Principle 2 and [Constraints and Dependencies](#constraints-and-dependencies) for the full regulatory acceptance requirement before deploying CLEAR in any government-regulated program context.

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:

- Integration architecture for CLEAR (CLEAR1 enterprise platform) as an external identity proofing and biometric authentication CSP
- Federation patterns for accepting CLEAR identity assertions via OIDC
- IdP-mediated integration pattern through the enterprise Identity Broker (PingOne)
- Biometric-anchored identity verification and proofing channel strategy (mobile app, in-person kiosk)
- Multi-vertical reuse architecture: member, provider, workforce, and service desk
- Repeat biometric authentication pattern for enrolled CLEAR users
- Privacy-preserving assertion acceptance — biometric results only, no raw biometric data
- Failover and graceful degradation for CLEAR service unavailability
- Healthcare-specific integration considerations (patient check-in, provider identity, workforce access)

**Out of Scope**:

- General identity proofing architecture and IAL framework (see GUID-SEC-IAM-PROOFING-2.2.05)
- Government/Medicaid regulatory acceptance determination (requires program-level policy and legal decision)
- ID.me integration architecture (see GUID-SEC-IAM-ID.ME-STRATEGY-2.2.10)
- Alternative CSP evaluation and vendor scoring (separate vendor assessment process)
- Identity proofing policy and regulatory requirements (see GUID-SEC-IAM-PROOFING-2.2.05)
- Security controls, configuration requirements, and compliance mandates (belong in `standards/security/`)
- Solution Building Blocks and implementation-specific configuration (Phase E–F)
- Commercial terms, pricing, and procurement (belong in sourcing artifacts)
- CLEAR-as-IdP integration patterns — CLEAR does not support operation as an enterprise IdP and cannot replace the enterprise Identity Broker in any deployment scenario; see Core Principle 1

### CLEAR Platform Overview

CLEAR (NYSE: YOU, operated by Alclear LLC) is a biometrics-powered identity verification company originally deployed for expedited physical security verification at airports, stadiums, and healthcare venues, and now expanding into digital identity verification for healthcare, enterprise workforce, and consumer access scenarios. [Confidence: 90/100]

CLEAR performs **multi-layered identity verification** combining biometric capture, government-issued document scanning and validation, and authoritative source corroboration. Per CLEAR's published documentation, all three layers are required at minimum: **Biometric Verification**, **Document Verification**, and **Source Validation**. Projects may be configured with additional controls to increase assurance for specific regulatory or business requirements. [Confidence: 97/100 — confirmed in CLEAR official documentation] This multi-layered model makes CLEAR functionally comparable to ID.me's document-plus-biometric approach, rather than a biometric-only alternative. CLEAR's primary differentiation is its **Known User Key Flow**: after a user completes first-time full verification and a CLEAR User ID (PSUID — a persistent identifier) is established, subsequent verifications can be completed with a selfie alone while CLEAR continues identity proofing and security validation across all verification vectors in the background. [Confidence: 97/100]

**CLEAR1** refers to CLEAR's enterprise B2B identity platform. The CLEAR1 designation was provided by the requesting architect; this document uses "CLEAR1" and "CLEAR" interchangeably to refer to the enterprise integration platform. Architects SHALL confirm the current product name and feature scope with CLEAR account teams before any implementation planning, as product naming and capabilities evolve. [Confidence in "CLEAR1" product name: 60/100]

### Enrolled Population and Ecosystem Leverage

CLEAR has built a consumer identity network through airport, venue, and healthcare deployments across the United States. Users who have previously completed full verification with CLEAR are issued a **CLEAR User ID (PSUID)** — a persistent identifier that links all future verifications to their established identity. When a CLEAR User ID is present, subsequent verification can use the **Known User Key Flow** (selfie-only), significantly reducing friction for returning users while maintaining full identity assurance in the background. [Confidence: 97/100 — confirmed in CLEAR documentation]

This enrolled population is a material architectural asset for high-frequency scenarios such as provider portal access and workforce authentication. Its alignment to benefit-program member demographics (Medicaid, CHIP) is less established than ID.me's government-benefit-user base and should not be assumed without demographic analysis of the specific program population. [Confidence: 72/100]

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-CLEAR-STRATEGY-2.2.11.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

**1. CLEAR Is a CSP, Not an IdP — The Identity Broker Is Architecturally Required**

CLEAR is a Credential Service Provider (CSP) that also provides a native OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorization server capability. In a direct OIDC integration, CLEAR acts as the OIDC issuer — applications redirect users to CLEAR's authorization endpoint and receive JWT identity tokens from CLEAR. [Confidence: 97/100 — CLEAR OIDC endpoint confirmed in official documentation]

However, this native OIDC capability does NOT mean CLEAR can substitute for the enterprise Identity Broker in Gainwell's architecture. Per [CLEAR's official Ping integration documentation](https://docs.clearme.com/docs/ping), the supported enterprise integration model is the **Ping Workflow Orchestration pattern** — CLEAR functions as a verification service node within a Ping workflow (Journey or DaVinci flow), not as an OIDC identity provider. Ping manages enterprise session authority; CLEAR returns verification results to Ping. The enterprise Identity Broker (PingOne) remains the session authority and token issuer for all enterprise applications. [Confidence: 97/100 — confirmed in CLEAR official documentation]

CLEAR's Ping integration is confirmed compatible with the following Ping platforms:

- **PingOne Advanced Identity Cloud** (Journey Node)
- **PingAM** (Journey Node)
- **PingOne DaVinci** (DaVinci Connector)

[Confidence: 97/100 — explicitly listed in CLEAR official documentation under "Works With"]

In Gainwell's enterprise deployment, the **PingOne DaVinci** orchestration engine is the preferred integration platform. CLEAR is deployed as a DaVinci connector node within identity verification flows. Ping invokes CLEAR, CLEAR performs verification, and CLEAR returns results to Ping.

Alternatively, CLEAR's native OAuth 2.0 / OIDC capability MAY be used as a **broker-mediated OIDC federation** pattern — PingOne acts as the relying party (RP) to CLEAR's OIDC authorization server, accepting CLEAR-issued JWT identity tokens and normalizing them into enterprise claims. This pattern is valid when DaVinci connector deployment is not feasible (e.g., legacy PingFederate environments, phased migration scenarios, or integrations requiring CLEAR's OIDC-specific claim payloads). The DaVinci connector remains the recommended approach due to its no-code configuration, built-in intelligent routing, and tighter User Profile Matching integration.

Regardless of integration mechanism (DaVinci connector or OIDC federation), all CLEAR integrations SHALL route through the enterprise Identity Broker. Direct application-to-CLEAR OIDC integration — where an application bypasses PingOne to accept CLEAR tokens directly as enterprise session credentials — is not consistent with the enterprise IdP consolidation strategy and SHALL require architecture review and exception approval before adoption.

Applications SHALL authenticate against the enterprise Identity Broker (PingOne). Applications SHALL NOT bypass PingOne to issue enterprise session tokens directly from CLEAR's OIDC endpoint.

**2. Regulatory Acceptance Validation Is Mandatory Before Government Program Deployment**

CLEAR does not hold Kantara IAL2 accreditation or FedRAMP authorization at the time of this document's authoring. [Confidence: 65/100 — this status may have changed; architects SHALL verify CLEAR's current certification status directly with CLEAR before any production planning.] Accordingly, CLEAR MAY NOT be deployed as an IAL2-equivalent CSP for any government-regulated program (Medicaid, CHIP, SNAP, or other Title XIX/XXI programs) without completing the following steps:

1. Obtain CLEAR's current certification documentation — Kantara accreditation status, FedRAMP authorization status, and any applicable state authorizations
2. Submit this documentation to the relevant program authority or state agency for formal review
3. Obtain written acceptance from the program authority confirming that CLEAR's proofing model satisfies the applicable IAL requirement
4. Record the acceptance in the enterprise risk register and the integration design documentation for the specific program

This requirement does NOT apply to non-government-regulated workflows where the enterprise defines its own assurance standard — workforce authentication, service desk identity, private-sector provider enrollment, and healthcare-adjacent access scenarios not subject to federal/state program IAL mandates. For those workflows, the enterprise MAY define CLEAR's biometric verification model as satisfying the enterprise-defined assurance requirement.

**3. Biometric Assertion Acceptance — Not Raw Biometric Data**

The integration architecture SHALL accept verified identity assertions from CLEAR — biometric binding confirmation, identity assurance level claims, and verified attribute attestations — rather than raw biometric data. The enterprise SHALL NOT receive, store, or process raw biometric templates from CLEAR. CLEAR retains custody of enrolled biometric data; the enterprise receives assertion results only. This design minimizes enterprise liability under BIPA (Biometric Information Privacy Act), HIPAA, and applicable state biometric privacy laws. [Confidence: 90/100 — consistent with privacy-preserving federation design and CLEAR's published data model]

**4. Biometric Channel Inclusivity and Mandatory Alternatives**

CLEAR's enrollment channels (mobile app biometric capture, in-person kiosk) represent a different accessibility profile from document-centric proofing. Some user populations cannot or will not complete biometric enrollment. The enterprise SHALL provide an alternative proofing pathway (e.g., ID.me, in-person supervised proofing) for all workflows where CLEAR is deployed. Designating CLEAR as the sole mandatory proofing channel for any required workflow is architecturally prohibited; an accessible alternative SHALL exist.

**5. Multi-Vertical Utilization as an Architectural Imperative**

CLEAR's enterprise commercial model assumes broad utilization across multiple user populations and use cases to achieve favorable unit economics. The architecture SHALL support CLEAR integration across member, provider, workforce, and service desk scenarios — not narrowly scoped to a single program. Narrow deployments that do not leverage multi-vertical reuse will produce materially higher per-user costs and may not justify the minimum commitment structure typical of CLEAR enterprise agreements. [Confidence: 68/100 — reflects the commercial model described in the provided comparison documents; specific commercial terms require validation with CLEAR and SHALL NOT be treated as authoritative from this document]

#### CLEAR Federation Integration Architecture

**Architectural intent**: Define the supported integration patterns for connecting the enterprise Identity Broker to the CLEAR platform, enabling identity assurance claims from CLEAR to flow into enterprise access decisions.

**Supported Integration Patterns** (in order of preference):

| Priority | Pattern | Mechanism | When to Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 (Preferred)** | DaVinci Connector | CLEAR DaVinci connector node within orchestration flow | New deployments; PingOne DaVinci environments; no-code configuration desired |
| **2** | Journey Node | CLEAR Journey Node within PingOne AIC or PingAM trees | Environments on PingOne AIC or PingAM without DaVinci |
| **3** | Broker-Mediated OIDC Federation | PingOne as RP to CLEAR's OIDC authorization server | Legacy environments; phased migrations; OIDC-specific claim payloads needed; DaVinci/Journey unavailable |
| **Prohibited** | Direct App-to-CLEAR OIDC | Application directly consumes CLEAR OIDC tokens | Never — bypasses broker session authority |

**Design guidance**:

- The enterprise SHOULD integrate CLEAR through PingOne DaVinci using the CLEAR DaVinci connector (available via the [PingOne DaVinci Marketplace](https://marketplace.pingone.com/item/clear-integration)). This is a **no-code integration** — the CLEAR connector is configured within DaVinci flows without custom application code. [Confidence: 97/100 — confirmed in CLEAR official documentation]
- For environments using PingOne Advanced Identity Cloud or PingAM, the CLEAR Journey Node ([Ping Marketplace](https://marketplace.pingone.com/item/clear)) provides equivalent functionality within Journey/Tree-based workflows. [Confidence: 97/100]
- Where the DaVinci connector or Journey Node is not feasible, CLEAR's native OAuth 2.0 / OIDC integration MAY be used with PingOne configured as the OIDC relying party. In this pattern, PingOne federates with CLEAR's OIDC authorization server, validates the CLEAR-issued JWT (signature, issuer, audience, timestamp), and normalizes CLEAR claims into enterprise tokens. This pattern requires additional configuration (OIDC client registration, claim mapping, token validation rules) compared to the connector approach.
- Regardless of integration mechanism, the Identity Broker SHALL validate CLEAR verification results — assurance level, CLEAR User ID, and verified attribute assertions — before issuing enterprise tokens
- All CLEAR integrations SHALL route through the enterprise Identity Broker. Direct application-to-CLEAR integration (where an application consumes CLEAR tokens without broker mediation) is architecturally prohibited.

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-CLEAR-STRATEGY-2.2.11.md#idp-mediated-integration-flow-pingone-davinci]

#### IdP-Mediated Integration Flow (PingOne DaVinci)

**Architectural intent**: PingOne DaVinci orchestrates the CLEAR interaction as a connector node within an identity verification flow, maintaining centralized session context and allowing CLEAR biometric verification to be incorporated into standard authentication flows without requiring application-level changes.

**Design guidance**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
autonumber
actor User
participant App as Application
participant Browser as "User Agent / Browser"
participant Broker as "Enterprise IdP / Broker (PingOne)"
participant DaVinci as "PingOne DaVinci Flow Engine"
participant CLEARNode as "CLEAR DaVinci Connector"
participant CLEAR as "CLEAR Verification Service"
participant Store as "Enterprise Identity Store (PingOne Directory)"

User->>App: Begin registration or access protected resource
App->>Browser: Redirect to enterprise broker
Browser->>Broker: Authentication request with application context
Note over Broker: Evaluate required IAL and AAL for transaction

alt Current session satisfies required assurance level
    Broker->>Browser: Return authorization response with enterprise token
    Browser->>App: Present code or token
    App->>User: Access continues

else First-time user — full verification required
    Broker->>DaVinci: Invoke DaVinci identity verification flow
    DaVinci->>DaVinci: Check user record for existing CLEAR User ID
    Note over DaVinci: No CLEAR User ID found → route to full verification
    DaVinci->>CLEARNode: Trigger CLEAR connector (Establish Identity Project ID)
    CLEARNode->>CLEAR: Initiate verification session (API Key + Project ID + user profile data)
    CLEAR->>Browser: Redirect user to CLEAR verification experience
    Browser->>CLEAR: User enters CLEAR verification flow
    CLEAR->>User: Biometric capture, document scan, and source validation
    User-->>CLEAR: Complete multi-layered verification
    Note over CLEAR: Perform User Profile Matching against provided user data
    CLEAR-->>CLEARNode: Return verification result + CLEAR User ID via webhook
    CLEARNode->>DaVinci: Pass verification outcome to flow
    Note over DaVinci: Map CLEAR User ID to enterprise user record
    DaVinci->>Store: Store CLEAR User ID against user identity record
    DaVinci->>Broker: Signal verification complete with assurance level
    Note over Broker: Apply IAL policy and issue enterprise token
    Broker->>Browser: Return authorization response with enterprise token
    Browser->>App: Present code or token
    App->>User: Registration or access continues

else Returning user — Known User Key Flow
    Broker->>DaVinci: Invoke DaVinci identity verification flow
    DaVinci->>DaVinci: Check user record for existing CLEAR User ID
    Note over DaVinci: CLEAR User ID found → route to Known User Key Flow
    DaVinci->>CLEARNode: Trigger CLEAR connector (Known User Key Project ID + CLEAR User ID)
    CLEARNode->>CLEAR: Initiate Known User Key session
    CLEAR->>Browser: Redirect user to selfie-only verification experience
    Browser->>CLEAR: User enters biometric re-verification flow
    CLEAR->>User: Selfie capture
    Note over CLEAR: Biometric match + background security validation across all vectors
    User-->>CLEAR: Complete selfie capture
    CLEAR-->>CLEARNode: Return re-verification result
    CLEARNode->>DaVinci: Pass re-verification outcome to flow
    DaVinci->>Broker: Signal re-verification complete
    Note over Broker: Validate result and evaluate session policy
    Broker->>Browser: Return authorization response with enterprise token
    Browser->>App: Present code or token
    App->>User: Access continues
end
```

- The DaVinci flow engine SHALL record the CLEAR transaction identifier, CLEAR User ID, and assurance level result in the enterprise identity store (PingOne Directory) for audit purposes; the broker issues enterprise tokens only after the DaVinci flow signals verification complete
- The broker SHALL normalize the CLEAR verification result attributes (received via DaVinci flow) to the enterprise canonical claim schema before issuing downstream tokens
- The CLEAR repeat biometric authentication path — available for users already enrolled with CLEAR — provides a materially faster re-authentication experience than knowledge-based or document-based flows. This path SHOULD be leveraged for high-frequency access scenarios (provider portal, workforce authentication, service desk) where re-authentication, not re-proofing, is the requirement

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-CLEAR-STRATEGY-2.2.11.md#davinci-clear-node-configuration-standard-integration-pattern]

#### DaVinci CLEAR Node Configuration (Standard Integration Pattern)

**Architectural intent**: Define the standard configuration and responsibility model for deploying the CLEAR DaVinci connector within an enterprise identity verification flow, based on [CLEAR's official Ping integration documentation](https://docs.clearme.com/docs/ping).

**Design guidance**:

**CLEAR Node Required Configuration** (per CLEAR official documentation):

| Parameter | Description | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| **Establish Identity Project ID** | CLEAR project identifier for full (first-time) identity verification flows | CLEAR Console — configured per use case |
| **Known User Key Project ID** | CLEAR project identifier for returning-user selfie-only flows | CLEAR Console — configured per use case |
| **API Key** | Authentication credential for CLEAR API calls from the DaVinci connector | CLEAR Console — securely stored in PingOne |
| **Custom Field** (internal org identifier) | Unique organizational identifier (e.g., Employee ID, Provider NPI, User ID) used for User Profile Matching | Enterprise — mapped from PingOne Directory |
| **First Name** | User's first name — improves User Profile Matching accuracy | Enterprise — mapped from PingOne Directory |
| **Last Name** | User's last name — improves User Profile Matching accuracy | Enterprise — mapped from PingOne Directory |
| **Date of Birth** (if available) | User's DOB — improves User Profile Matching accuracy | Enterprise — mapped from PingOne Directory (when applicable) |

**Responsibility Separation** (per [CLEAR official documentation](https://docs.clearme.com/docs/ping)):

| Domain | CLEAR Responsibility | Ping (DaVinci) Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| **Identity Verification** | Performs biometric capture, document verification, and authoritative source validation | N/A — CLEAR owns verification decisioning |
| **User Profile Matching** | Matches verified user to the enterprise user record using provided profile data and custom field | Provides user profile data to CLEAR; stores match result |
| **Known User Key Flow** | Determines eligibility; performs selfie-based re-verification with background assurance | Checks for CLEAR User ID on user record; routes to appropriate flow |
| **Workflow Orchestration** | N/A — CLEAR is a verification service, not an orchestrator | Defines when CLEAR verification occurs within the identity journey; configures pre/post actions |
| **Credential Management** | Issues API Key and Project IDs via CLEAR Console | Securely stores and manages CLEAR credentials within DaVinci connector configuration |
| **Intelligent Routing** | N/A | Determines which CLEAR flow (full verification vs. Known User Key) based on presence of CLEAR User ID on user record |
| **Data Mapping** | Returns CLEAR User ID and verification attributes | Maps CLEAR output attributes to PingOne Directory user record fields |
| **Data Storage** | Retains biometric data and verification records | Persists CLEAR User ID and verification metadata on enterprise user record |

**Enterprise Use Cases** (confirmed in CLEAR documentation):

- **Onboarding** (RECOMMENDED as initial touchpoint): Introduce CLEAR during employee/provider/member onboarding to establish CLEAR User ID early; all subsequent use cases benefit from Known User Key Flow
- **Multi-Factor Authentication**: CLEAR biometric selfie as a step-up authentication factor within DaVinci MFA flows
- **Conditional Access**: Risk-based policies trigger CLEAR re-verification for sensitive resource access
- **Password Reset**: CLEAR biometric verification as identity confirmation during self-service password reset
- **Account Recovery**: CLEAR re-verification to confirm identity before account recovery actions

**DaVinci Flow Design Pattern** (standard injection points):

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User Initiates Action] --> B{Authentication Required?}
    B -->|No| Z[Continue to Application]
    B -->|Yes| C[PingOne DaVinci Flow Starts]
    C --> D{Check User Record}
    D -->|CLEAR User ID exists| E[Route to Known User Key Flow]
    D -->|No CLEAR User ID| F[Route to Full Verification Flow]

    F --> G[CLEAR Node: Establish Identity Project]
    G --> H[User Completes CLEAR Verification]
    H --> I{Verification Successful?}
    I -->|Yes| J[User Profile Matching]
    I -->|No| K[Handle Failure / Offer Alternative Path]
    J --> L[Store CLEAR User ID on User Record]
    L --> M[Map Verified Attributes to Directory]

    E --> N[CLEAR Node: Known User Key Project]
    N --> O[User Completes Selfie Verification]
    O --> P{Re-verification Successful?}
    P -->|Yes| M
    P -->|No| Q[Escalate to Full Verification or Deny]

    M --> R[DaVinci Signals Verification Complete]
    R --> S[Broker Issues Enterprise Token]
    S --> Z

    K --> T{Alternative CSP Available?}
    T -->|Yes| U[Route to ID.me or In-Person Proofing]
    T -->|No| V[Deny Access / Manual Review]
```

**Standard Deployment Steps** (per CLEAR documentation):

1. **Configure the CLEAR Node**: Provide Establish Identity Project ID, Known User Key Project ID, API Key, custom field mapping, and user profile attributes within the DaVinci flow
2. **Validate in Test Environment**: Deploy the flow to a test group and validate: user verification, User Profile Matching, CLEAR User ID storage, Known User Key Flow routing for returning users, and data mapping persistence
3. **Launch**: Deploy to production and make the CLEAR experience available to the target user population

> **Integration characteristic**: This is a **no-code integration**. Teams can configure CLEAR credentials into the DaVinci connector without custom application development. Change management, employee/provider communications, and socialization SHOULD be planned as part of the rollout. [Confidence: 97/100 — confirmed in CLEAR official documentation]

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-CLEAR-STRATEGY-2.2.11.md#ial-to-application-mapping]

#### IAL-to-Application Mapping

**Architectural intent**: Define how application-declared identity assurance requirements are enforced through broker routing logic when CLEAR is the designated CSP, consistent with the IAL framework in GUID-SEC-IAM-PROOFING-2.2.05.

**Design guidance**:

- Applications SHALL declare their minimum required IAL during broker registration, per GUID-SEC-IAM-PROOFING-2.2.05
- The broker SHALL normalize CLEAR assurance claims to the enterprise IAL schema using a defined claim mapping; CLEAR-specific assurance claim values SHALL NOT be passed raw to downstream applications
- For government-regulated applications requiring IAL2: the broker SHALL enforce the regulatory acceptance prerequisite defined in Core Principle 2 before issuing IAL2-backed tokens using CLEAR assertions. Token issuance to government program applications SHALL be blocked until program authority written acceptance is documented and recorded
- IAL claim persistence: CLEAR assurance results SHALL be recorded in the enterprise identity store with the proofing event timestamp. Re-proofing triggers SHALL align with GUID-SEC-IAM-PROOFING-2.2.05 re-proofing policies. Any deviation from the default re-proofing interval SHALL be evaluated against applicable regulatory requirements and documented as a formal exception — biometric anchoring does not by itself constitute grounds for extending the interval

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-CLEAR-STRATEGY-2.2.11.md#biometric-proofing-channels-and-enrollment-model]

#### Biometric Proofing Channels and Enrollment Model

**Architectural intent**: Define how CLEAR's biometric enrollment model integrates with the enterprise proofing workflow, accounting for its different accessibility profile compared to document-centric CSP flows.

**Design guidance**:

- CLEAR supports two primary enrollment channels: (a) in-person kiosk enrollment at physical CLEAR locations (airports, healthcare facilities, and other CLEAR deployment sites) and (b) mobile app-based digital enrollment via the CLEAR mobile application. [Confidence: 85/100]
- The integration SHALL support both enrollment entry points; existing CLEAR members SHALL NOT be required to re-enroll
- For new enrollees without CLEAR memberships, the mobile app pathway provides the primary digital option; in-person kiosk enrollment provides the higher-assurance physical option
- The enterprise SHALL communicate available CLEAR enrollment channels to users before redirecting; users must have a clear path to channel selection before the flow begins
- For users unable or unwilling to complete biometric enrollment, an alternative proofing pathway SHALL be available per Core Principle 4

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-CLEAR-STRATEGY-2.2.11.md#provider-and-workforce-identity--multi-vertical-reuse-pattern]

#### Provider and Workforce Identity — Multi-Vertical Reuse Pattern

**Architectural intent**: Define the architectural pattern for extending CLEAR integration beyond member proofing to provider enrollment and workforce authentication, activating the platform economics that justify an enterprise commitment.

**Design guidance**:

- CLEAR's enterprise model supports multi-vertical utilization; the same enrolled user identity MAY be reused across member, provider, and workforce access scenarios without re-proofing, subject to application IAL requirements and session policy
- Provider identity workflows MAY leverage CLEAR for verified personal identity as part of enrollment; mapping CLEAR-verified personal identity to provider credential records (NPI registry, CAQH, state licensing records) is an enterprise orchestration responsibility at the broker or application layer — not a CLEAR responsibility
- Workforce access scenarios (employee authentication, service desk, VPN) have materially higher session frequency than member enrollment; CLEAR's fast biometric re-authentication is architecturally advantageous in these contexts
- The enterprise SHALL model projected utilization volumes across all intended verticals before contract execution to ensure commitment levels reflect realistic demand

[strategy/guidance/security/Identity/GUID-SEC-IAM-CLEAR-STRATEGY-2.2.11.md#privacy-and-biometric-data-minimization]

#### Privacy and Biometric Data Minimization

**Architectural intent**: Ensure the CLEAR integration minimizes data collection and transmission, with explicit handling for biometric data under BIPA, HIPAA, and applicable state biometric privacy laws.

**Design guidance**:

- Raw biometric templates SHALL NOT be transmitted from CLEAR to the enterprise; the integration is assertion-based only
- The enterprise SHALL document which CLEAR attribute scopes are requested for each application integration; requesting scopes beyond application requirements is prohibited
- Biometric data use agreements with CLEAR SHALL explicitly define permitted use purposes; enterprise use of CLEAR identity assertions for purposes beyond the defined scope is prohibited
- A HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with CLEAR SHALL be in place before deploying CLEAR for any workflow involving ePHI-adjacent identity verification (patient check-in, member enrollment, provider access to clinical applications). Whether CLEAR qualifies as a Business Associate under HIPAA for a given workflow requires legal review of the specific data flows. [Confidence: 78/100 — BAA requirement is standard HIPAA practice; BAA availability from CLEAR requires contractual confirmation]
- A Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) covering biometric data collection, retention, and sharing SHALL be completed and maintained as a prerequisite for production integration
- Deployment in states with biometric privacy laws (Illinois BIPA, Texas CUBI, Washington WFBR, and emerging state laws) requires state-specific legal review of CLEAR's consent, retention, and deletion practices before production use

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

- **Identity Pillar**: CLEAR's biometric-anchored identity provides a strong Zero Trust identity signal — physiological binding resists credential theft, replay attacks, and synthetic identity fraud more effectively than knowledge-based or document-centric proofing alone. Where regulatory acceptance is established, this strengthens the identity signal underpinning Zero Trust policy.
- **Device Pillar**: CLEAR's mobile enrollment model creates a natural pairing between the enrolled device and the biometric identity. The mobile device used for biometric capture becomes a contextual signal supporting continuous device-identity binding, adding depth to Zero Trust device posture evaluation.
- **Applications Pillar**: Multi-vertical CLEAR reuse across member, provider, and workforce applications enables consistent Zero Trust access policy without separate proofing events per application, reducing friction while maintaining assurance.
- CLEAR integration is one identity assurance input to Zero Trust policy; the broker's policy engine uses the CLEAR assurance claim alongside device posture, risk score, and context in access decisions — consistent with GUID-SEC-IAM-REF-2.2.01 Zero Trust alignment guidance.

### Constraints and Dependencies

- **CLEAR Is Not an IdP — Broker Is Architecturally Mandatory** *(Critical)*: CLEAR does not function as an Identity Provider. It cannot issue enterprise identity session tokens, cannot manage authentication state, and cannot be configured as an enterprise IdP in any deployment scenario. This is a platform capability boundary, not a policy restriction. Every CLEAR integration SHALL flow through the enterprise Identity Broker (GUID-SEC-IAM-IDENTITY-BROKER-2.2.02), which issues all enterprise tokens. Solution architects and application teams SHALL account for this dependency at design time; retrofitting broker-mediated integration after a direct-integration design is costly and architecturally unsound.

- **Identity Broker Dependency**: This ABB depends on GUID-SEC-IAM-IDENTITY-BROKER-2.2.02; all CLEAR integration SHALL flow through the enterprise Identity Broker. Direct application-to-CLEAR integration is prohibited.

- **Regulatory Acceptance Prerequisite** *(Critical — Government Programs)*: Deployment of CLEAR for government-regulated programs requires completion of the four-step regulatory acceptance process defined in Core Principle 2. This is a hard architectural gate. Token issuance to government program applications using CLEAR assertions SHALL be blocked until written program authority acceptance is documented.

- **BAA and Legal Agreement Prerequisites**: A HIPAA Business Associate Agreement, biometric data use agreement, and Privacy Impact Assessment with CLEAR SHALL be completed and active before any production deployment in healthcare-adjacent workflows.

- **CLEAR Certification Currency**: CLEAR's SOC 2 Type II certification and other applicable compliance certifications SHALL be reviewed prior to contract execution and monitored during the integration lifecycle. Integration SHALL be suspended if material compliance gaps emerge. [Confidence: 72/100 — SOC 2 is publicly referenced; current scope requires verification with CLEAR]

- **IAL Framework Dependency**: This ABB depends on GUID-SEC-IAM-PROOFING-2.2.05 for the IAL policy framework, assurance level definitions, and proofing record retention requirements.

- **Commercial Commitment and Utilization Modeling**: CLEAR's enterprise pricing requires a multi-year minimum commitment. The enterprise SHALL complete a utilization modeling exercise across all intended verticals before contract execution. [Confidence: 40/100 on specific commercial terms in the provided comparison documents — these are AI-generated market estimates and SHALL be confirmed through direct commercial negotiation. Do not use figures from the comparison documents in procurement documentation without independent verification.]

- **State Biometric Privacy Law Compliance**: Deployment in states with biometric privacy laws (Illinois BIPA, Texas CUBI, Washington WFBR, and emerging state laws) requires state-specific legal review before production use.
